correctness.rationale: For stationary dyadic-piecewise-constant initial density the shell process is a genuine time-homogeneous Markov chain by conditional uniformity. A nearest-neighbor first-passage decomposition gives t=z(p+qt²) and R=z(qt+p/(2-t)); two-degree algebraic conjugation proves R nonrational for pq>0. Finite-state HMM word-gap sequences always have rational matrix-resolvent generating functions, giving impossibility and infinite Hankel rank. Singularities at both ±(2 sqrt(pq))^{-1} and a pole at 2/(4−3p) yield rigorously separated three-regime positive-return asymptotics, including parity. Six rational parameters and 25 return lengths each were independently checked by exact killed-chain and coefficient recurrences, together with finite large-n diagnostics; computation does not replace analytic proofs.

value.rationale: The first binary digit is a canonical coarse observable for this elementary random interval map. It has full binary shift support, but the exact stationary output has unbounded predictive/hidden-state complexity in the strong sense that no finite-state HMM can reproduce even its return-gap probabilities; this is not a finite-sample failure and persists through all 1/2<p<1, contrasting with the pure doubling endpoint. The exact excursion-tail phase structure gives a useful quantitative description of why finite models cannot be exact. Novelty and reproducibility are not the sole grounds for value: the result identifies an exact obstruction to a natural class of symbolic statistical reductions.
